To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed and tested a combined oligonucleotide and immunostaining protocol for the detection of Gordona in environmental samples and that the ribosomal rRNA content of Gordona cells was variable.
we have combined a polyclonial antibody stain with a rRNA-targeted oligonucleotide for the single cell identification of species of the Gordona.
the combined use of oligonucleotide probes and immunostaining provides an improved detection limit and high specificity for the detection of Gordona in single cells of activated sludge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods for the detection of microorganisms in environmental samples.
the development of a novel method for the in situ detection of microbial species in environmental samples.
the detection of Gordona in the environment and the development of methods for their identification and quantification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combined immunostain/oligonucleotide probe approach can be applied for the detection of Gordona in environmental samples.

the use of oligonucleotide probes in combination with immunostains is a promising approach that can be used in the future to study microbial populations that cannot be detected by either method alone.
the combined use of immunostaining and oligonucleotide probes is a promising approach to improve the detection of microorganisms in environmental samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combined use of immunostaining and oligonucleotide probes for the simultaneous detection of microorganisms in situ is an effective tool that can be used to study the physiology of microorganisms in complex microbial consortia.
we have combined the advantages of two different staining methods to improve the sensitivity of detection of a specific group of bacteria.
oligonucleotide probes are useful for the detection of active microorganisms, whereas polyclonal antibody stains can be used to detect non-viable or slowly growing microbial populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined use of immunostains and oligonucleotide probes is an attractive approach for the detection of microorganisms in complex environments.

the combined use of immunostaining and ribosomal RNA targeted in situ hybridization is a useful strategy to detect low abundance populations of microorganisms in activated sludge, especially those with low metabolic activities.
oligonucleotide probes are not always superior to antibody probes.
